current_pain_severity.diagnosis: CRITICAL FRICTION: The current firmware rejects 76.2% of non-English and punctuated business names globally (HTTP 400). Names like 'McDonald\'s' or 'São José' fail completely.

options.A_LEN_CHARS_VS_BYTES: Confusion between character length (len) and IEEE 802.11 octet limit (32 bytes). Multi-byte UTF-8 causes buffer overflows or hard cuts.
options.B_OVER_AGGRESSIVE_ASCII_FILTER: Filter `c < 32 || c > 126` bans all accented Latin, CJK, Cyrillic, and Arabic.
options.C_QUOTE_BAN_BLOCKING_COMMERCE: Banning single quote (') breaks thousands of global brand names (McDonald's, Domino's, L'Occitane).
options.D_ALL_OF_THE_ABOVE: Comprehensive design mismatch between web form validation and physical 802.11 beacon framing.

principles: 1. Byte-Safe Length Clamp: IEEE 802.11 strictly limits SSIDs to 32 BYTES, not 32 characters. Multi-byte chars must be counted in UTF-8 bytes.

2. Dual-Layer Naming (SSID vs Portal Title): Decouple 'Wi-Fi Broadcast SSID' (max 32 bytes, ASCII/safe UTF-8, no quotes) from 'Portal Header Title' (unlimited UTF-8, full accents, emojis, full candidate/business name).

3. Intelligent Auto-Transliteration: When the merchant types 'Padaria São José • Pão Quentinho', the system automatically sets Title to 'Padaria São José • Pão Quentinho' and suggests SSID 'Padaria Sao Jose' (safe, universal, 100% compatible across all OSs).
4. Quote Normalization: Convert apostrophes / quotes (' or ") to spaces or clean hyphens for SSID, while keeping pristine typography in the captive portal HTML.
5. Safe UTF-8 Flag: Enable ESP32 802.11 UTF-8 SSID broadcast bit for deployments in CJK/Arabic regions while enforcing the <= 32 byte boundary.
